correctness.rationale: The pointed extension-mask signature exactly implements standard EF rank-three equivalence; a direct recursive EF game agreed on 901 pairs. For every path of at least seven vertices its pointed rank-two types depend only on distance-to-endpoint truncated at three, hence \(P_n\equiv_3P_7\). Componentwise three-round EF composition truncates each path multiplicity to at most three, yielding \(4^7-1=16{,}383\) exhaustive canonical cases. Two separately coded algorithms both return 160 distinct signatures and a sharp maximum minimum representative of 23, with explicit witness \(2P_1\sqcup P_2\sqcup P_3\sqcup P_4\sqcup P_5\sqcup P_7\). The symbolic cutoff ensures these finite checks prove the unbounded statement.

value.rationale: Finite linear forests form a natural maximum-degree-two acyclic graph family. The complete rank-three quotient of 160 classes and sharp 23-vertex uniform kernel are natural structural classification and optimal finite-model bound, not a trivial single-path threshold or arbitrary small-order check. The result gives an exact finite test domain for all rank-three sentences on this infinite class and identifies a non-obvious six-component extremizer. No stronger general theorem is claimed.
